html:
Guayaquil is the largest city and chief port of Ecuador, on the Guayas River near the Pacific. From the late 1800s it grew rich as the world's leading port for cacao, the bean of chocolate.

Founded by the Spanish in the 1530s and settled at its present site by 1547, it had shipyards that built vessels for the Pacific coast. It declared its independence on 9 October 1820. Estates in the lowlands behind it grew cacao for the chocolate makers of Europe, and around 1900 Ecuador was the largest cacao exporter in the world.

The cacao planters and merchants of Guayaquil backed the liberal politics of Eloy Alfaro against the conservative highlands of Quito. Plant diseases and falling prices ruined the trade in the 1920s, and bananas later took its place. The story ties back to the first use of cacao in the region.
sum: Guayaquil is the largest city and chief port of Ecuador, on the Guayas River near the Pacific. From the late 1800s it grew rich as the world's leading port for cacao, the bean of chocolate.
